questions.question: Give an account of Yersinia pestis infection, including its epidemiology, mode of transmission and prevention.
questions.solution_html:

  • transmission and prevention.
  • - Yersinia pestis is a Gram-negative bacterium that causes plague. , found in rodents and
  • other small mammals. , - It spreads mainly through the bite of infected rat fleas

  • lymph nodes. . - Prevention includes rodent and flea control, sanitation and early
  • antibiotic treatment.

questions.solution_html:
• Amastigote: Round or oval-shaped, non-flagellated, found inside human macrophages.
  • Promastigote: Elongated in shape; has a single anterior flagellum.- Found in the gut of

questions.question: Explain how environmental factors influence the occurrence and transmission of disease.
questions.solution_html:
• Climate change affects the survival of disease-causing organisms and vectors. Deforestation
  • increases contact between humans and wildlife. Water pollution spreads waterborne
  • diseases. Poor sanitation increases infectious disease transmission. Urbanisation and
  • overcrowding favour disease spread. Floods and droughts increase the risk of disease
  • outbreaks.

questions.solution_html:

  • Confirms suspected infections. Monitors disease outbreaks.Detects antimicrobial resistance.

questions.question: Explain the role of fruit bats in the transmission of Nipah virus.
questions.solution_html:
• Fruit bats are natural reservoirs of Nipah virus. They shed the virus through saliva and urine.
  • Contaminated fruits and date palm sap can transmit the virus. Humans may become
  • infected by consuming contaminated food. Infection can spread from animals such as pigs to
  • humans. Human-to-human transmission occurs through close contact with infected
  • persons.
